goal: Give the client a persistent left-rail navigation sidebar (trips, expandable to their legs, plus standalone flights, with an active-route highlight) mounted inside AppShell only, turn Home into a lightweight landing view backed by the data /api/trips and /api/flights already return, relocate Home's multi-select flight table and its combine / new-trip / add-to-trip / export-KML toolbar to a new /flights page so no existing capability is lost, and paginate TripDetail's legs table client-side at exactly 20 rows per page over the array interleaveTripRows already produces, with the page number carried in ?page= via the existing useSearchParams instance. Client-only: no file under src/ changes, no new endpoint, no schema change.
frozen_decisions: Sidebar scope: sidebar *replaces* `Home`'s combined table as primary nav. `Home` becomes a lightweight landing/dashboard, not the trip/flight browser.

Legs pagination: 20 legs per page, implemented client-side (windowing the array already returned by `GET /api/trips/:id`) — explicitly not a backend/API change. The realistic case is "dozens of legs," not thousands; no requirement to optimize for 100+-leg trips beyond correct paging.
Design step is skipped: both features wire up existing contracts only. There is no design.md for this run — `ctx.sh design` has nothing to return and tasks must not wait for one.
getTripById's eager point-track loading is out of scope. No task may add a ?points=0 flag or lazy per-leg loading.
Never touch the user's running server on port 3000 or the live flights.db. Verification runs on another port against a copy.
sequencing_rationale: No server change is needed and none is planned. The sidebar's two data sources (GET /api/trips, which already embeds each trip's flights with points stripped, and GET /api/flights) are exactly the two calls Home.tsx makes today at lines 24-27, and the standalone-flight set is the `tripFlightIds` computation already at Home.tsx:161-163. Pagination slices `interleaveTripRows(trip.flights, trip.planned_legs)`, an array TripDetail already holds in full. Any task that finds itself editing a file under src/ has hit a frozen decision and must stop and escalate rather than proceed.

Three phases, because the shared file (client/src/index.css) means these tasks can never run in parallel anyway, and a reviewer gate between them is the only thing that makes the overlap safe. Phase order is chosen so the tree is shippable at every gate — this matters more than usual here: the user's live server serves client/dist off disk, so `npm run build:client` (needed to verify anything) immediately changes what their browser gets on reload.
Phase 1 is pagination: the smallest, most isolated change (one page component, a handful of CSS lines), independent of the layout rework, and it lands user-visible value in one short reviewed step.

Phase 2 makes the sidebar exist and work while Home is left completely alone. Navigation therefore ships *before* the browser it replaces is dismantled — the escape-hatch-first ordering. If phase 3 never landed, the app would still be fully usable.

Phase 3 dismantles Home: the table and its toolbar move verbatim to a new /flights page, Home becomes the landing view, the sidebar gains its 'All flights' entry, and README is corrected. This is the only phase that can lose functionality, so its reviewer is opus.

FLAGGED — a scope call the Orchestrator should sanity-check with the user: the frozen decision retires Home's combined table, but that table is also the only home of four capabilities the README documents (Combine Selected, New Trip from selection, Add to Trip, Export KML for a flight set — README lines ~203 and ~324-335). Deleting them was not asked for, so T-005 moves them intact to /flights rather than dropping them. This does not re-litigate the frozen decision (the sidebar, not that table, is primary nav) but it does add one route and one page beyond the literal wording of the intake. If the user would rather those actions live somewhere else, say so before phase 3 starts — it is cheap now and expensive after.

tasks.title: Paginate TripDetail's legs table at 20 rows per page, page number in ?page=
tasks.goal:
Window the legs table in client/src/pages/TripDetail.tsx to 20 rows per page, client-side, over the existing `mergedRows` array. Do not change what is fetched. Implement exactly this, do not improvise an alternative: 1. `const LEGS_PER_PAGE = 20;` at module scope, next to LEG_COLORS (TripDetail.tsx:11). 2. Reuse the component's existing `useSearchParams()` instance (line 23) — do not call the hook a second time. Derive `const pageCount = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(mergedRows.length / LEGS_PER_PAGE))` and `const page = clamp(parseInt(searchParams.get('page') ?? '1', 10) || 1, 1, pageCount)`. A missing, non-numeric, zero, negative or too-large value must clamp silently — never throw, never render an empty table, never rewrite the URL on its own. 3. `const pageRows = mergedRows.slice((page - 1) * LEGS_PER_PAGE, page * LEGS_PER_PAGE);` and render `pageRows` in the tbody instead of `mergedRows`. The empty-state row still keys off `mergedRows.length === 0`. 4. A `setPage(n)` helper that mirrors `setView` (TripDetail.tsx:89-94) exactly: copy searchParams, `params.set('page', String(n))` or `params.delete('page')` when n === 1, then `setSearchParams(params, { replace: true })`. `replace: true` is deliberate and matches the ?view= precedent — it also gives the required Back behaviour, since leaving the page for /flight/:id and pressing Back returns to the URL that still carries ?page=N. 5. Controls render *only* when `mergedRows.length > LEGS_PER_PAGE`, immediately after the inside .legs-section, as `
` containing: a Prev button (disabled at page 1), the text `Page {page} of {pageCount} · legs {from}–{to} of {mergedRows.length}`, and a Next button (disabled at the last page). No numbered page buttons. Style it in client/src/index.css in the house idiom — plain CSS appended near .legs-section, reusing .btn/.btn-ghost, no new colour values that are not already in the file. 6. Do NOT change ghost-row reorder semantics: `canMoveUp`/`canMoveDown` keep deriving from the leg's index in `sortedPlannedLegs` (the whole trip), not the page window, so a ↑ that moves a leg across a page boundary still works and the leg simply appears on the adjacent page. 7. client/src/components/PlannedLegRows.tsx is in allowed_paths but is not expected to change; interleaveTripRows stays pure and page-unaware. Also write two reusable checkers into the run's tools/ directory (they are run artifacts, not application code): tools/scratch-server.sh (the recipe verbatim from the plan's sequencing_rationale) and tools/seed-many-legs.mjs, which takes a scratch database path and creates one trip holding exactly 45 flights by direct better-sqlite3 INSERT (read the trips/flights DDL in src/db.ts; src/ is read-only context here).
